title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache cost model (Alpenglow Payments)
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran an Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and caching (prefix/KV cache) and a cost model tailored to Alpenglow's payments use case. We covered expected throughput improvements from batching, KV cache hit rate sensitivity, potential 40-70% token cost reduction with caching+batching, and follow-up benchmark pilot on their test traffic. Security items (SAML, KMS, audit logs) briefly discussed; next steps: share pricing spreadsheet, run 2-day benchmark, provide SOC2+security pack.
transcript:
Header: Recorded 2026-03-16 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (SE), Priya Nair (Alpenglow), Daniel Ortiz (Alpenglow), Laura Chen (Alpenglow)

00:00 Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm sofia from redwood, i'll hand over to marcus for the optimize walkthrough — we scheduled 45 but we have up to an hour, cool?
00:08 Marcus: great thanks sofia. hi priya, daniel, laura. quick agenda: batching basics, prefix cache vs kv cache, hit-rate/cost model, recommended configs for payments use-cases, and then next steps and benchmark plan.
00:23 Priya: sounds good, our main goal is to reduce per-transaction latency under 120ms P95 while shaving token cost. we've got a couple of million transactions a day, median prompt length is 180 tokens, few long form refunds are ~1k tokens.
00:40 Marcus: ok that profile is super common for payments support flows. quick baseline question: are you currently using hosted endpoints or self-hosted?
00:48 Daniel: hosted, we call our provider's managed endpoints today. cost is creeping up, latency is inconsistent during peak hours.
00:56 Marcus: understood. so batching helps by increasing GPU amortization — for example when you batch 8 requests at a time we often see 2.8x throughput improvement for short sequences. that gives you lower per-token cost but can add a small tail latency.
01:15 Priya: how small? our SLO is 120ms P95 for the user-facing flow, backend can tolerate 250ms in some cases.
01:23 Marcus: with smart routing and adaptive batching you can keep P95 within target — we do dynamic batch windows: if queueing time reaches 8ms we flush, otherwise we wait up to 12ms for additional requests. in practice for your qps profile that should keep P95 < 200ms in hosted mode; dedicated gives tighter guarantees.
01:42 Laura: you mentioned KV cache — short explanation? i've seen prefix cache mentioned too.
01:47 Marcus: sure — prefix (or deterministic prefix) cache stores repeated prompt prefixes and reuses cached KV states so generation jumps straight into decoding for the suffix, which is great if you have highly templated prompts. KV cache is more general: it stores KV entries for recent contexts and can span user sessions; hit rate depends on dialogue similarity. we sometimes call it K-V cash in transcriptions (laughs).
02:12 Daniel: our flows are templated for verification steps but have free-text user complaints, so mix of structured + unstructured.
02:20 Marcus: that's the sweet spot for hybrid approach — prefix caching on static templates (welcome text, instructions) + KV cache for session continuity. in cost terms, in our model we assume prefix cache can shave ~30-50% of tokens for templated requests, and KV cache hit rates of 20-45% depending on session reuse give additional savings.
02:41 Sofia: quick note on quant numbers — these are modeled, real numbers vary, so we propose a short benchmark.
02:48 Priya: yes please. can you run the benchmark on a sample of our traffic?
02:52 Marcus: absolutely — typical pilot is 48h with 3 configs: baseline (no caching, small batching), optimize-1 (prefix cache + batching 4-8), optimize-2 (prefix + KV cache + dynamic batching). we'll gather P95 latency, mean tokens per request, and cost delta.
03:10 Priya: sweet. show us the cost math?
03:15 Marcus: sure, i'll walk through a simplified cost model we use. baseline: assume 180 tokens per call * 3M calls/month = 540M tokens. at our hosted rate of $0.50 per 1M tokens (example numbers for model family X), that's $270/mo. with batching only, if you reduce per-token infra overhead you might see 10-20% dollar savings due to better GPU utilization. with prefix cache (30% token reduction on 60% of calls) plus KV cache (20% hit overall), combined you could reduce bill by roughly 40-70% depending on hit rates and batching efficiency.
04:02 Daniel: that's a big swing. are those numbers with dedicated pricing assumptions?
04:06 Marcus: the percent improvements are tech-agnostic; absolute $ differ. dedicated reserved capacity gives lower per-token infra costs and stricter latency SLOs, so your bill could be more predictable but requires commit. hosted is easier to trial.
04:18 Laura: security - we need SAML SSO, KMS integration, audit logs for any PII touches — do you support customer-managed KMS?
04:26 Sofia: yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs, plus SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC. we'll share our security pack and SOC2 artifacts after the call.
04:38 Priya: do you redact PII in transit or at rest?
04:41 Jordan: redwood leaves that to customer policy, but we provide per-route data retention settings and can disable retention + apply encryption keys you manage. we'll include specifics in the security pack.
04:55 Marcus: back to cost modeling — important sensitivity: KV cache hit rates have diminishing returns after ~60% because cache storage and invalidation costs grow. also long-tail prompts (1k tokens) dominate cost if they are common — they need special handling (streaming, suffix-only generation, or separate heavy model).
05:20 Priya: for refunds flow long prompts are 10% of calls but 60% of tokens consumed.
05:27 Marcus: exactly — in the benchmark we'll isolate heavy flows and measure their contribution; often solution is route long calls to a higher-token-optimized model and keep short templated flows on the cached/dedicated pool.
05:40 Daniel: question about orchestration — can we route by policy like latency-first for external UX and cost-first for background jobs?
05:48 Marcus: yes, smart routing policies let you route by latency, cost, region, or tier. you can set automatic fallbacks; e.g., if dedicated pool saturates we fallback to hosted but with lower model variant.
06:05 Priya: any gotchas on request shaping or prompt design we should do?
06:10 Marcus: trim unnecessary system tokens, move static instructions into the prefix cache, and consider compressing user history by summarization to keep token counts down. also consider batched embeddings for similarity pipelines rather than many small calls.
06:28 Sofia: we prepared a small sample cost spreadsheet for alpenglow — marcus i'll share the assumptions now. (screen share noises)
06:36 Marcus: here's the sheet. baseline assumptions: 3M monthly calls, avg 180 tokens, model cost $0.50/1M tokens, batch gain factor 2.8x on throughput, KV hit rate scenarios 15/30/45%. for each scenario we compute adjusted tokens and estimated monthly cost.
06:55 Priya: can you email that sheet after the call with editable assumptions?
06:58 Sofia: yes i'll send it, we'll include knobs for QPS, avg tokens, KV hit, prefix coverage, and dedicated discount factor.
07:05 Daniel: what's the expected engineering work to run a 48h benchmark?
07:09 Marcus: minimal — we need a sampling hook on your side to replay traffic, or you can provide a 48h sample payloads. we need network allowlist, and a test API key. if you prefer private deployment we can run the pilot in your VPC but that'll take more setup.
07:26 Laura: network allowlist is fine, but we need to review the security docs first.
07:30 Sofia: we'll send security pack + the benchmark runbook.
07:33 Marcus: one more note on latency: batching is orthogonal to KV cache. you can have batching and still benefit from a warm KV cache; the scheduler will try to maximize both. sometimes caching reduces variance so batching flush thresholds can be tuned lower.
07:51 Priya: ok let's talk timeline: we want a pilot in the next 2 weeks and decision by end of month.
07:56 Sofia: doable — we'll target sending materials today, benchmark next week, and 2-week evaluation.
08:02 Priya: are there any competitors we should be aware of for similar features?
08:06 Marcus: others like OpenAI's edge/embeddings offerings and Anthropic have caching strategies but fewer production-grade controls around routing and dedicated autoscaling; AWS Bedrock is more infra-centric.
08:20 Priya: good to know.
08:24 Marcus: ok wrapping up recap in a second.
08:26 Sofia: recap: 1) send cost spreadsheet + security pack (Sofia) 2) set up 48h benchmark (Marcus + Alpenglow engineering), 3) draft pilot runbook and allowlist (Jordan), 4) follow-up meeting after results to decide dedicated vs hosted.
08:44 Priya: thanks all. any final Qs?
08:47 Daniel: one small: will caching affect model behavior / hallucination rates?
08:51 Marcus: caching just reduces repeated prefix tokens being recomputed; it doesn't change the underlying model weights. prompt engineering and reranking handle hallucination control; we'll include recommended evals.
09:03 Sofia: thanks everyone we'll follow-up with notes and materials.
09:08 End of recording
